decisions.rationale: The full name 'Duchenne muscular dystrophy' refers to one specific disease with no further categorization, used in the title as the locus reference.
'Duchenne' on its own is not a disease mention; it only denotes a disease when paired with Becker muscular dystrophy, and splitting it causes information loss.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 - Contiguous text strings (Duchenne example)

decisions.rationale: 'Becker muscular dystrophies' refers to the single specific disease Becker muscular dystrophy; the plural describes affected patients and does not denote a family of diseases.
'disease' is a very general term that is explicitly excluded from annotation.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms

decisions.rationale: 'dystrophic syndrome' is a generic descriptive phrase built on the general term 'syndrome' and does not name a specific disease or a defined disease family.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms

decisions.rationale: 'Duchenne / Becker muscular dystrophy' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases, so it is annotated as one Composite Mention.
'Duchenne muscular dystrophy' is a disease name used to modify the noun 'gene' (the human DMD gene), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'DMD' is the abbreviation of the disease, separately annotated as a synonymous mention, and it modifies 'gene' in this context, so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 - Modifiers and 6 - Synonymous mentions

decisions.rationale: 'DMD' appears as a disease name used in 'the gene homologous to DMD' and is not a standalone noun phrase, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'myopathies' refers to a family of multiple distinct muscle diseases, so it is a Disease Class.
'Emery Dreifuss muscular dystrophy' names one specific disease with a single definition and no further categorization.
'DMD' modifies the noun 'homologue' ('the DMD homologue'), so it is used as a disease-name Modifier.
